properties.name: Gravity Research Foundation
properties.who: Roger Babson; the Gravity Research Foundation
properties.what was claimed or done: Founded by the economist Roger Babson, after his essay 'Gravity—Our Enemy Number One', to find ways to shield against or reduce gravity.
properties.what came of it: Wikipedia calls its early efforts 'crankish'; it later turned to understanding gravity and now runs a yearly essay award.
properties.where: Wellesley, Massachusetts, as Wikipedia gives it

properties.name: Thomas Townsend Brown's 'gravitator' and electrogravitics
properties.what was claimed or done: Reported that high-voltage asymmetric capacitors lost weight; built 'gravitator' devices, coined 'electrogravitics' and patented the idea in Britain (1928).
properties.what came of it: Later tests in vacuum found the force was ion wind, ordinary propulsion, not anti-gravity (NASA Glenn Research Center, 2004).

properties.name: Paul Alfred Biefeld (Biefeld–Brown effect)
properties.what was claimed or done: Co-namesake of the Biefeld–Brown effect, the claimed weight loss of charged capacitors.
properties.what came of it: The effect is explained as ion wind.

properties.name: US Office of Naval Research report on Brown's 'Electro-Gravity Device'
properties.what was claimed or done: A report on Thomas Townsend Brown's 'Electro-Gravity Device'.
properties.what came of it: Wikipedia cites it among its references only.
properties.where: the Office of Naval Research, Arlington, Virginia

properties.name: US Air Force study of the Biefeld–Brown effect (R. L. Talley)
properties.what was claimed or done: A funded study testing for a force from high-voltage capacitors.
properties.what came of it: No force above the detection limit of 2 × 10⁻⁹ newtons.

properties.name: Henry Wallace's spinning-disc patents
properties.what was claimed or done: US patents claiming spinning brass discs make a 'gravitomagnetic' field.
properties.what came of it: 'No independent testing or public demonstration ... is known.'

properties.name: Hayasaka and Takeuchi's spinning gyroscope
properties.what was claimed or done: Reported in Physical Review Letters that a gyroscope spinning one way weighed less.
properties.what came of it: A test a year later found nothing (Nitschke and Wilmath, 1990).

properties.name: Nitschke and Wilmath's test of spinning gyroscopes
properties.what was claimed or done: Tested whether a spinning gyroscope changes weight.
properties.what came of it: 'Null result for the weight change of a spinning gyroscope' (Physical Review Letters).

properties.name: Douglas Torr's gravitomagnetic fields in superconductors
properties.who: Douglas Torr, University of Alabama in Huntsville
properties.what was claimed or done: Papers proposing that a changing magnetic field could make detectable gravity-like fields in superconductors.
properties.what came of it: No reproducible example has been accepted.

properties.name: Eugene Podkletnov's spinning superconductor
properties.what was claimed or done: Claimed a fast-spinning superconducting disc reduced the weight of things above it by 0.3 to 2 percent.
properties.what came of it: Many attempts to reproduce it, NASA researchers' among them, had negative results.
properties.where: Tampere University of Technology, Finland, where he worked

properties.name: Ning Li and AC Gravity LLC
properties.what was claimed or done: Claimed a superconducting disc could levitate a bowling ball and a working 'AC Gravity' prototype (Popular Mechanics, 1999); AC Gravity received a $450,000 US Department of Defense grant in 2001.
properties.what came of it: 'No further evidence of this prototype has been offered.'

properties.name: NASA Breakthrough Propulsion Physics Program
properties.what was claimed or done: Studied 'far out' propulsion, anti-gravity among it.
properties.what came of it: Found no evidence of anti-gravity forces; such approaches were listed as non-viable.
properties.where: NASA Glenn Research Center, Cleveland, Ohio, which ran it

properties.name: NASA Glenn's test of asymmetric capacitors
properties.what was claimed or done: Tested Brown-style 'lifters' for thrust.
properties.what came of it: No thrust without ion wind.
properties.where: NASA Glenn Research Center, Cleveland, Ohio

properties.name: University of South Carolina 'gravity generator'
properties.who: Douglas Torr and Timir Datta, University of South Carolina
properties.what was claimed or done: A leaked document (confirmed to Wired) said the university planned to patent and license a 'gravity generator'.
properties.what came of it: No further public information followed.

properties.name: Jonathan Campbell's test of Brown-type effects
properties.what was claimed or done: An experiment on Biefeld–Brown effects.
properties.what came of it: Explained as ion wind; no thrust in vacuum.

properties.name: Martin Tajmar's tests
properties.who: Martin Tajmar (with M. Kößling and O. Neunzig, 2024)
properties.what was claimed or done: Tested steady electric fields in vacuum for anti-gravity effects.
properties.what came of it: No effects in vacuum; he argues the Biefeld–Brown effect is corona wind.
properties.where: TU Dresden, Germany, where he works

properties.name: Institute for Gravity Research, Göde Scientific Foundation
properties.what was claimed or done: Tried to reproduce many anti-gravity experiments and offered a one-million-euro reward for one that can be reproduced.
properties.what came of it: 'All attempts ... have been unsuccessful thus far.'

properties.name: CERN: does antimatter fall up?
properties.what was claimed or done: Compared antihydrogen escaping from the top and bottom of a vertical vacuum chamber.
properties.what came of it: Ruled out repulsive gravity between antihydrogen and Earth.

properties.name: US Navy 'Craft Using an Inertial Mass Reduction Device' patent
properties.who: Salvatore Pais, US Department of the Navy
properties.what was claimed or done: A patent for a craft that would reduce its inertial mass; approved after the Navy's chief technology officer called it feasible.
properties.what came of it: Physicists call the engineering implausible (it needs unreachable field strengths and power); the patent lapsed in 2018 for non-payment.
properties.where: Naval Air Warfare Center, Patuxent River, Maryland, where Pais worked

properties.name: Frederick Alzofon's nuclear-spin theory
properties.what was claimed or done: Proposed that aligning nuclear spins could reduce inertia; bench tests in the 1990s claimed up to 17 percent temporary weight loss.
properties.what came of it: Never peer-reviewed or reproduced; far from mainstream physics.

properties.name: Hal Puthoff's metric engineering
properties.what was claimed or done: A paper on engineering spacetime, the framework behind the Navy patent.
properties.what came of it: Needs negative energy density, never shown in any lab.
properties.where: SRI International, Menlo Park, California, with which the article associates him

properties.name: Exodus Propulsion Technologies
properties.what was claimed or done: Reported a 40-gram electrostatic unit giving thrust equal to its weight, without propellant; plans an orbital test on a cube satellite.
properties.what came of it: The explanation offered seems to contradict basic electrostatics and the patent filing has physics errors, though a real force may have been measured.

properties.name: Falcon Space and the Alternative Propulsion Energy Conference
properties.what was claimed or done: Researches propellantless propulsion, testing past anti-gravity claims (nuclear-spin alignment, superconductors); hosts the conference, with live 'anti-gravity' experiments in 2021.
properties.what came of it: No result reported.

properties.name: Hoverr Inc
properties.what was claimed or done: Received a $275,000 US National Science Foundation small-business grant for its design.
properties.what came of it: No result reported.
properties.where: California; the article names no city

properties.name: AGES Tech
properties.what was claimed or done: Researching anti-gravity propulsion systems.
properties.what came of it: No result reported.
properties.where: Australia; the article names no city

properties.name: Lindgren, Kovacs and Liukkonen's geometric electromagnetism
properties.who: Jussi Lindgren, Andras Kovacs, Jukka Liukkonen
properties.what was claimed or done: A theory paper predicting gravity-like effects in spinning superconductors (Journal of Physics: Conference Series).
properties.what came of it: Theory only; no experiment.

note: Compiled for the Culprits map, round 210o, from the sources named in each entry. Places are the institution or town each source names; entries whose source names no place have no position.
